SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to

What this means
In this part you learn to Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to.
3. Make one local Kenya example of Reading from your county, market, farm, or school.
4. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP2 learner study Reading?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. when reading?
2. How do you turn pages of (1 HRS) orientation when reading pictures that drag and drop from a book when reading?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Demonstrate top-bottom left to right in a digital clip. orientation skills when • Learners could be engaged in a reading picture walk activity and guided to.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
